title: The N-1 property descends from a Laurent ring to the Noetherian domain
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a Noetherian domain R, if the Laurent ring R[z, z to the minus one] is N-1, then R is N-1 as well (statement lines 45451-45455). The proof does not exhibit a finite generating set for the integral closure directly: it nests the two integral closures, uses normality of the Laurent ring over the fraction field to bound S' inside it, writes finitely many Laurent expansions of the generators, and shows that R' lies in the finite R-module generated by the finitely many coefficients, invoking Noetherianity at the end (proof lines 45457-45471). Choosing the coefficient module as the witness of finiteness is the substance, and the author writes the reduction out. H2.
